sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year, from $23.7 billion in FY2016 to $51.8 billion in FY2025 [F168][F1][F10], though table revenue differs from each year's own 10-K for every year from FY2016 to FY2025 [R1][X1][X10].
The path was boom and bust: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 [D161], then rose 153.2% in FY2021 [D200].
Revenue rose 76.5% to $61.0 billion in FY2022 [D238][F7], mainly on higher realized prices and Shell Permian volumes [P59].
FY2023 revenue fell 20.5% to $48.5 billion [D274][F8] as lower realized prices outweighed higher volumes [P47].
Lower 48 supplied 70.2% of FY2025 revenue [D711] and added 8.0pp of growth [D713], more than the total 4.9% increase [D342].
Sales rose $4,199 million: volumes added $6,197 million, including Marathon Oil, while lower realized crude prices took $4,615 million [P28][D342].
Crude oil, 66.3% of FY2025 revenue [D551], added only 0.1pp of growth [D553].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% [D352] against 4.9% revenue growth [D342], so operating leverage was negative.
Basic EPS fell 18.7% [D344], faster than the 13.6% decline in net income [D343], while diluted shares rose 6.1% [D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025 [F30], below its 17.9% window median [D831]; the pack has no operating margin, so net margin carries this section.
Cost of revenue rose to 37.9% of revenue [D326] from 36.6% [D292].
Production and operating expenses rose $1,580 million, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition [P24].
The largest move, a 43.1pp net margin rise in FY2021 [D208], came with cost of revenue falling from 42.0% to 37.6% of revenue [D143][D179]; the cited passages do not explain that cost move.
Operating cash flow was $19.8 billion in FY2025 [F59], 2.48x net income [D333].
Operating cash flow fell 1.6% [D346] because lower commodity prices outweighed the Marathon Oil operations added [P6].
Free cash flow is absent from the pack after FY2022, when it was $18.2 billion [F73], or 0.97x net income [D227] against a 0.98x window median [D840].
FY2021 operating cash flow rose 253.9% [D201] on higher realized prices and Concho-related volumes [P51].
Net cash was $7.11 billion in FY2025 [D337], up from $6.13 billion [D303], or 12.1% of revenue [D338].
Among six energy peers, net cash as a share of revenue ranks at the 100th percentile [D850] against a -7.7% peer median [D851].
The current ratio of 1.30x [F153] sits between the 1.25x window low [D841] and the 1.45x median [D843].
Buybacks of $5.02 billion [X141] and dividends of $4.00 billion [X151] totalled $9.01 billion [D339], 46% of operating cash flow [P31][F59].
Diluted shares rose 6.1% to 1,253.4 million [D356][X131] after a 2.1% fall in FY2024 [D322]; the cited filings do not explain the increase.
Table revenue differs from each year's own 10-K for every year from FY2016 to FY2025 [R1][X1][X10], so growth rates across the table may mix presentations.
Net income fell three years running: 41.3% in FY2023 [D275], 15.6% in FY2024 [D309] and 13.6% in FY2025 [D343]; the three-year CAGR is -24.7% [D845].
Cost growth outpaced sales in FY2025, so the Marathon Oil integration is the test of whether earnings recover.
Net margin returning above its 17.9% window median [D831] would confirm recovery, while a fall below the FY2025 level of 15.4% [F30] would reverse it.
Disposals reaching the $5 billion target by year-end 2026 [P32], from $3.2 billion in 2025 [P32], would confirm the funding of the $9.01 billion return [D339].
Operating cash flow holding at or above $19.8 billion [F59] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the FY2025 base.
